clue.text: Break new ground in school

definitions.meaning: to drag a spiked frame over ploughed soil, breaking up the clods
the famous English public school in north-west London

explanation.definitionFit: A farmer breaks up tilled earth with a spiked implement of that name, and the same word names a famous English boarding school.

clue.text: Music appropriate to church in one of the services

parts.note: an air is a tune or piece of music
for means suited or appropriate to, as in 'right for'
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Music suitable for church in one of the armed forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The aviation branch is one of the armed services alongside army and navy.

clue.text: High-level murder detectives discovered in climbing mountain

indicators.note: the detectives are found inside the turned mountain
in a down clue climbing means the word reads upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Eiger is a famous Swiss Alpine peak
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police

explanation.surface: Detectives find a high-profile killing on a mountain climb.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' reads the mountain upwards to give REGIE; 'discovered in' is the container signal. 'High-level' hints at killing a king, not a mountaintop.
explanation.definitionFit: The killing of a king is about as high-ranking a murder as there is.

clue.text: Activity in which a wet pool is involved? That's about right

definitions.text: Activity in which a wet pool is involved? That's about right

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go about the letter for right
involved signals the letters of a wet pool are twisted together

explanation.surface: A sport played in a wet pool; that seems correct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A WET POOL and 'about' wraps those letters round R; the whole clue is also the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A team ball game swum in a pool is exactly an activity involving wet water.

clue.text: Quicker way to stop circuit court imprisoning you in hearing

parts.note: to short an electrical circuit is to make it fail, stopping it

indicators.note: the court abbreviation locks up the next piece, holding it inside
the word you, spoken, is heard as the letter U

parts.note: the pronoun you

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a faster route for halting proceedings in a circuit court where the accused is detained.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoning' puts U inside CT; 'in hearing' tells you YOU is taken by its sound, the letter U. 'Quicker way to' — 'to' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A path that saves time over the usual route is exactly what the phrase means.

clue.text: Daily surfacing of fish on river test produces new business

indicators.note: in a down clue the first pair sits on top of the river and test

parts.note: the Sun is a British daily newspaper
anglers call fish coming up to feed at the surface a rise
the Indus is a great river of south Asia
a try is an attempt or test

explanation.surface: Fish rising daily on a river being tested leads to a new business.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SUN is a British tabloid newspaper, hence 'Daily'.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising new sector of the economy, such as early electronics, still in its dawn.

clue.text: Commons speeches omitting nothing at first

indicators.note: the word for nothing is left out of the speeches
at first places the dropped letter at the very start

parts.note: orations are formal speeches
O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Speeches in the House of Commons leave out nothing at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commons' looks like Parliament but means shared food allowances, as in a college.
explanation.definitionFit: Commons are provisions shared out to a group, so fixed food allowances.

clue.text: A party connected with, e.g., American red or blue state

parts.note: red or blue is a colour, spelt the American way
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A party linked with American red and blue politics in a swing state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'red or blue state' suggests US politics, but red or blue is just a COLOR in American spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Colorado is a US state in the Rocky Mountains.

clue.text: Sit there, improperly in casual wear

indicators.note: improperly signals sit there is to be arranged wrongly into new order

explanation.surface: Someone told to sit there is improperly dressed in casual clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: A short-sleeved cotton top is a staple of informal dress.

clue.text: In bog, given proper scare

indicators.note: the word for proper is placed in the word for bog

parts.note: a fen is a marsh or bog
right means proper or correct

explanation.surface: Someone stuck in a marsh gets a proper fright.
explanation.definitionFit: To frighten someone is to give them a fright, the verb sense of scare.

clue.text: Post-war leader about to drive across line

indicators.note: the two words for being about to drive are laid across the line letter, holding it

parts.note: a golfer about to drive is at the tee, giving AT TEE

explanation.surface: A leader after the war is about to drive a car over a line on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about to drive' is golf: a golfer ready to drive stands at the tee. Clement Attlee was the British Prime Minister elected in 1945.
explanation.definitionFit: Clement Attlee led Britain's Labour government in the years straight after the Second World War.

clue.text: Agreement I follow to produce musical works

indicators.note: the letter I comes after the word for agreement

parts.note: acting in concert means acting in agreement

explanation.surface: Once a deal is struck, I go on to compose some music.
explanation.definitionFit: Concertos, in the Italian plural, are compositions for soloist and orchestra.

clue.text: Out, say, after three

indicators.note: say signals the word is to be taken by its sound when spoken

parts.note: forth means out or outwards, as in 'go forth'

explanation.surface: Someone is out, as it were, after the count of three.
explanation.definitionFit: The ordinal that comes next after third in a sequence.

clue.text: Philosophical fellow is on edge, oddly

indicators.note: oddly signals the letters of is on edge are arranged in a strange order

explanation.surface: A thinker behaves strangely because he is nervous and on edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek Cynic thinker who lived in a barrel and searched for an honest man with a lamp.

clue.text: Found prophet endlessly restricting attempt

indicators.note: the shortened prophet hems in the word for attempt
endlessly means the prophet's name loses its last letter

parts.note: Elisha was an Old Testament prophet, successor to Elijah
a stab is an attempt

explanation.surface: A prophet tries to hold back his attempt to found something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves ELISH; 'restricting' is the container signal. 'Found' is the verb meaning set up, not the past tense of find.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up, the verb sense not the past tense of find.

clue.text: Money paid, over time, to entertain lavishly

indicators.note: the word for money paid goes over the time letter, covering it

parts.note: a fee is money paid for a service

explanation.surface: A fee, paid in overtime, funds some lavish entertaining.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, to honour or celebrate someone with festivities and generous hospitality.

clue.text: Part of Henry IV, as a last resort, included in some folios

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are put inside the folio letters

parts.note: F is folio and FF folios, so several folios give the letters F and FF

indicators.note: resort means sort again, so the letters of a last are rearranged

explanation.surface: As a last resort, a part from Shakespeare's history play is found in old folios.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resort' gives ALSTA (the anagram of A LAST), and 'included in' is the container; 'as' is just a link. The folio letters sit on both sides.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir John, the fat knight, is a role in Shakespeare's two Henry IV plays.

clue.text: Meat cooked in two ways for sporting colleague

indicators.note: cooked means the letters of meat are prepared in a new order
the same word is rearranged a second, different way

explanation.surface: Meat prepared two ways for a fellow sportsman.
explanation.walkthrough: MEAT is rearranged twice, once as TEAM and once as MATE.
explanation.definitionFit: A fellow member of the same side in a game.

clue.text: Piano solo's beginning, frequently

indicators.note: the beginning of solo's is its first letter

parts.note: oft is an old word meaning often or frequently

explanation.surface: A pianist frequently starts a solo on the piano.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piano' is the musical direction meaning quietly, not the instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, piano is the instruction to play quietly.

clue.text: Breaking off due to strain of second trial

parts.note: a court hearing is a trial

explanation.surface: A rift caused by the stress of a second court case.
explanation.definitionFit: In engineering, a shearing force snaps material by sliding layers apart under stress.

clue.text: Golding's novel released before autumn

indicators.note: the released word goes before the autumn word

parts.note: free means released
fall is the American word for autumn

explanation.surface: A Golding book is released ahead of the autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: William Golding wrote a 1959 book of this title.

clue.text: Chapter on spinner not particularly good

indicators.note: in an across clue the chapter letters come on, after, the spinner and not

parts.note: a top is a spinning toy
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chapter about a spinner bowler is not especially good.
explanation.definitionFit: Excellent or first-rate, an informal term of praise for quality.

clue.text: Mug investing most of capital in terrible deal, initially

indicators.note: the shortened capital goes in between the two initials
initially takes the first letters of terrible and deal
most of drops the last letter of the capital

parts.note: Ankara is the capital of Turkey

explanation.surface: A fool puts most of his capital into a terrible deal at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is a drinking vessel, not a dupe; 'investing' is a link that fits the money surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A large drinking cup, usually with a handle, for beer.

clue.text: Financial wrongdoing concealed by boards I'm on? Yes

indicators.note: the run of letters sits concealed inside the words boards I'm on yes

explanation.surface: A director wonders whether the boards he sits on hide fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: The buying or selling of church offices, a corrupt trade in sacred positions.

clue.text: Never having experienced loss, like a spoilt child?

definitions.meaning: a team that has never lost a match
a child who has never been smacked, hence spoilt

explanation.definitionFit: A side with no defeats has this record, and whimsically a child never given a thrashing might be spoilt.

clue.text: Artist repeatedly stopping at biblical mount

indicators.note: the repeated artist stops up the word at, sitting inside it

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the artist abbreviation is used twice over

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a crossword artist

explanation.surface: A painter keeps stopping at a mountain from the Bible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeatedly' doubles RA to RARA and 'stopping' plugs it into AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Noah's Ark came to rest on the mountains of this name in Genesis.

clue.text: Secret society bringing racket back in island

indicators.note: the turned racket word is placed in the society word

parts.note: a triad is a Chinese secret criminal society

indicators.note: back tells you the word for racket is read in the other direction

parts.note: din means noise or racket

explanation.surface: A secret gang brings its crooked racket back to an island.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' gives NID, and 'in' is the container signal; 'bringing' is a link. A Triad is a Chinese criminal secret society.
explanation.definitionFit: The larger island of the Caribbean nation it shares with Tobago.

clue.text: Successful period that could make one ladyfied

indicators.note: the answer's letters could be rearranged to make the clue word, so the shuffle runs in reverse

explanation.surface: A good spell that might turn a person into a lady.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse anagram: rearranging the answer's letters would make 'ladyfied', so you rearrange 'ladyfied' to find it.
explanation.definitionFit: A time of great success or enjoyment, originally a day of military manoeuvres.

clue.text: Very euphoric, and extremely lively

parts.note: high means euphoric or elated

indicators.note: extremely means take the letters at the extremes of lively, its first and last

explanation.surface: Someone is very euphoric and extremely lively.
explanation.definitionFit: As an adverb, to a great degree or exceedingly.
